title: Doorbell Predicts Rewards — activity cover
note: Cover: everything essential inside the middle 75% of the width, because the library card and the map rail crop it to a centred square. A hand resting flat on her chest is the calm-greeting picture; a hand hooked into her collar is restraint, which is a different lesson and the one a generic prompt draws.
scene: The entry hall, near the closed charcoal front door but with the door pushed to the edge of the frame — this is a portrait of the pair, not of the door. The handler kneels on one knee so her face is level with Lucy's, the two of them close together and turned toward each other, near enough that a square crop of the middle of the picture holds both faces comfortably. Her near hand rests open and flat on Lucy's chest, below the collar — the palm laid against the fur, fingers relaxed and pointing down. It is a resting touch, not a hold: no finger is hooked under the collar, she is not gripping the fur, and there is no tension anywhere in the arm. Lucy sits square, leaning very slightly toward her, ears soft, mouth closed, looking at the handler's face. The black leash is clipped to the collar ring and drops away slack out of the bottom of the frame; give it a thin lighter outline where it passes near her coat, and keep it off her back and shoulders. Both figures and the touching hand sit well inside the middle 75% of the width — nothing that matters may sit in the outer eighth on either side. Background: the lavender wall, one baseboard line, a sliver of the closed door at the edge. No guest, no doormat, no bed.
mustBeTrue: the handler's hand lies flat and open against Lucy's chest below the collar with no finger hooked under it and no grip on the fur, the two faces are level with each other and both fully inside the middle 75% of the width, and Lucy sits square and relaxed looking at the handler's face.
